question: For $f:\mathbb{R}\to[1,\infty)$ defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$, determine whether an arbitrary element $y$ of the co-domain has a real pre-image.
explanation:
Step 1: Take an arbitrary $y\in[1,\infty)$. Then $y\ge1$.
Step 2: To find a pre-image, solve $f(x)=y$, giving $x^2+1=y$.
Step 3: Hence, $x^2=y-1$. Since $y\ge1$, we have $y-1\ge0$.
Step 4: Therefore, real values $x=\sqrt{y-1}$ or $x=-\sqrt{y-1}$ exist and satisfy $f(x)=y$.
Step 5: Thus, every element of the given co-domain has at least one real pre-image.
Final Answer: Yes, every $y\in[1,\infty)$ has a real pre-image; hence, $f$ is onto.

options.A: Yes; $x=\pm\sqrt{y-1}$ gives a real pre-image, so $f$ is onto
options.B: Yes; $x=\pm\sqrt{y+1}$ gives a real pre-image, so $f$ is onto
options.C: No; $y=1$ has no real pre-image, so $f$ is not onto
options.D: No; elements greater than $1$ have no real pre-images
